paths.description: Entry page, global navigation, latest-updates listing, search entry, preferences, responsive behavior, performance, security, and discoverability. Represents the primary listing template.
Search results for “Disclosure Day”, representing search and discovery.
Disclosure Day movie detail, representing content/detail pages and metadata.
Quality-selection page reached from the movie detail. The audit inspected choices but did not transfer a media file.
Request Movies auxiliary journey, representing simple informational/support pages.
Representative missing route to assess HTTP and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture; computed styles report color-scheme: normal and a white body under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface/text colors with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rule and the primary journey uses full MPA navigations between search, detail, and download-step pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } with a reduced-motion-safe fallback and stable view-transition names for shared page chrome.

findings.summary: Long catalog pages provide no scroll-state orientation.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 10,169 CSS px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state/progress behavior and the header does not react to scroll.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative scroll progress or scroll-state-aware compact header for long listings.

findings.summary: Navigation gives little orientation between listing, detail, and download steps.
findings.evidence: The detail and download pages expose no breadcrumb trail; navigation is an abrupt full-page swap and only a footer Home link restores hierarchy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible breadcrumbs and directional transition/target highlighting so users can follow listing → detail → quality selection.

findings.summary: Reusable listing components depend on global sizing rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container usage; cards are reused across home/category surfaces and only adapt through page-level layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards a containment context and use size container queries where their image/text arrangement changes.

findings.summary: Many mobile controls are far below recommended touch-target size.
findings.evidence: At 360px, prominent links are 15–17px tall and search controls 27px tall; Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px with spacing, while retaining visible :focus-visible outlines.

findings.summary: The not-found state is a dead end.
findings.evidence: A real missing URL returns a bare “404 Not Found” page with no Home, search, retry, or related-content link.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an on-brand 404 with search, Home, category navigation, and a concise recovery message while preserving HTTP 404.

findings.summary: Mobile loading misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3,928ms and FCP 3,696ms; the trace’s warmer/unthrottled run measured 1,581ms, showing network conditions dominate.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the redirect chain, prioritize the first meaningful image, and defer below-fold images to bring mobile LCP below 2.5s.

findings.summary: Redirects and eager image delivery make the critical path unnecessarily heavy.
findings.evidence: The HAR records two redirects (fast → dad → soccer), 46 requests and 2.40MB transferred, of which 2.22MB is images; Lighthouse estimates 2,820ms redirect savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Redirect the requested host directly to the canonical host, lazy-load below-fold covers, and prioritize only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Analytics ships avoidable unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 66KiB unused JavaScript in the single Google Tag Manager resource, which transfers about 170KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only the analytics functionality used, defer it until consent/idle, or replace the full tag payload with a smaller endpoint.

findings.summary: Search lacks an accessible name and two image links have no text name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the label audit for #searchInput; DOM recon found the logo and Telegram anchors have empty text, relying on image semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visible label (or robust accessible name) to search and ensure every linked image exposes a concise link purpose.

findings.summary: Core links, metadata, and search controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 80 failing contrast nodes, including red-on-cornsilk at 3.75:1, white-on-orange at 3.21:1, and the search field at 2.1:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose text/background tokens that meet 4.5:1 for normal text and verify every state with automated and visual checks.

findings.summary: Some templates render text too small and cramped for comfortable reading.
findings.evidence: The request page screenshot renders dense instructions at extremely small scale; homepage body text is 15px with normal line-height and navigation links are often 13px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a fluid readable base size, at least ~1.5 line-height for prose, and responsive spacing/measure on auxiliary templates.

findings.summary: Reflow works, but touch-target sizing fails inclusive use.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout has no overflow, yet the target probe found dozens of 15–27px-high controls and Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target padding/spacing without introducing overflow and test at narrow viewport and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Many images are distorted or lack intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 34 incorrect-aspect-ratio images; the image primitive found 40 of 77 missing width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratios with correct width/height attributes and object-fit only where intentional.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals conflict with the live host.
findings.evidence: The requested .fast host redirects through .dad to .soccer, pages expose no rel=canonical, while sitemap URLs use the stale .scot host.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical hostname, redirect every alias directly to it, emit self-referencing canonicals, and regenerate sitemap URLs on that host.

findings.summary: Movie detail pages omit structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail page has no JSON-LD despite representing a Movie, and the homepage lacks og:url/canonical metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Movie JSON-LD on detail pages and complete canonical Open Graph metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Analytics runs on load without visible user control or demonstrated minimisation.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; the load screenshot shows no privacy choice, while GTM transfers ~170KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics behind informed consent where required, minimize events and retention, and batch or remove low-value collection.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: No clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or HSTS was present on the final document.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback), strict referrer and permissions policies, CSP, and HSTS at the edge.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling provides no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The tested missing route returns HTTP 404 but renders only server-default text with no navigation or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a resilient custom error template with Home/search links, retry guidance, and preserved status codes.

findings.summary: Multilingual catalog intent is not matched by translation-ready layout.
findings.evidence: The site advertises many language catalogs but fixes html lang to en-in, has no dir, and CSS inspection found ten physical left/right declarations with no locale UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep per-page lang accurate, support dir, replace physical positioning with logical properties, and make shared strings translation-ready.

findings.summary: Release dates use one hard-coded English presentation.
findings.evidence: Movie information renders “12 Jun 2026” while the site serves multiple language audiences and exposes no locale-aware formatting path.
findings.suggestedFix: Store machine-readable dates and format them with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the selected/document locale.

findings.summary: The image catalog wastes substantial transfer and decoding work.
findings.evidence: All 77 images use legacy PNG/JPEG; 36 are oversized, 37 lack srcset, and Lighthouse estimates 1,622KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes, correct dimensions, and appropriately sized thumbnails.

findings.summary: Below-fold content is fetched eagerly.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 74 below-fold images without loading=lazy, contributing to 2.22MB image transfer on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold covers and defer non-critical fetches until content approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party and media weight is disproportionate for a text-and-thumbnail listing.
findings.evidence: The initial page transfers 2.40MB: 2.22MB images plus ~170KB GTM, with 45 requests classified third-party relative to the requested alias.
findings.suggestedFix: Canonicalize the host, establish a page-weight budget, optimize/lazy-load media, and reduce analytics payload.
